newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Sick Austria president doesn't have AIDS, cancer.
newsitem.headline: Sick Austria president doesn't have AIDS, cancer.

text.p: Austrian President Thomas Klestil, admitted to hospital two weeks ago with an illness baffling doctors, is suffering from neither AIDS nor cancer, his spokesman said on Friday.

Klestil, 63, was unconscious for three days and hooked up to an artificial respirator last weekend following a deterioration in his illness, but doctors said on Monday his condition had stabilised and he was showing some improvement.
"He has been making satisfactory progress," presidential spokesman Heinz Nussbaumer told Austrian news agency APA. "His heart and circulation are working normally."
Asked whether Klestil was suffering from AIDS or cancer, Nussbaumer answered with an emphatic "No".
"There is not the least suspicion that he is either infected with the HIV virus or has cancer," he added.
Chancellor Franz Vranitzky took over as acting head of state on Monday on the request of the president.

Klestil, who separated from his wife in 1994 after issuing a public statement on his affair with his aide, Margot Loeffler, was admitted to hospital on September 13 and transferred to intensive care a week ago.
Doctors have only acknowledged that the president is suffering from a form of pneumonia, saying tests were still being carried out to determine the nature of a lung inflammation.
The specialist medical team at Vienna General Hospital were severely criticised on Monday for failing to alert government leaders as soon as the president fell into unconsciousness.
Under the constitution, the chancellor assumes the duties of president for 20 days, after which responsibilities pass in turn to the three presidents of parliament.
Klestil was elected in 1992 for a six-year term and has won plaudits for repairing the harm done to Austria's image abroad by the controversy over his predecessor Kurt Waldheim.
Waldheim, a former U.N. secretary-general was shunned by the international community following reports that he had failed to give a full account of his role in Hitler's Third Reich army.
